brief:
Two Israeli ministers this week floated proposals for the mass removal of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, according to Al-Monitor. The proposals resurface an idea voiced repeatedly by right-wing politicians over the past three years as they seek to shape policy ahead of elections.

The timing reflects intensifying political pressure within Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition as the electoral calendar tightens. Right-wing partners have revived displacement proposals at a moment when debate over Gaza's postwar governance and the status of its population has sharpened. The renewed calls signal the influence of hardline voices on coalition dynamics in the approach to voting.
